Source Detail: A verse becomes a household food rule; later the rule quietly disappears.
Narrative Function: Loyalty can hide inside ordinary food.
Game Use: A pantry comment can trigger two conflicting recollections of why milk vanished.

Source Detail: A blunt grandmother answers grand revelation with practical sarcasm.
Game Use: Nora tosses coins on the table when Abel offers a sweeping theory.

Source Detail: Grandma fills her fridge with skim, whole, chocolate, and other milk after Abel condemns it.
Narrative Function: Small domestic objects become political lines.
Game Use: A refrigerator inventory tells the player who disagrees before dialogue begins.

Source Detail: Grandma offers to take the child to Arizona and put her in school; muddy boots and animal chores complicate the fantasy.
Narrative Function: Leaving is practical and emotional at once.
Game Use: A ride offer is interrupted by the player remembering the trough and animals.

Source Detail: A favorite story explains that shouting can be affectionate in the family’s own code.
Game Use: A newcomer mistakes rough banter for a fight; later a real threat sounds almost identical.

Source Detail: A family memory turns a tiny color choice into a symbol of respectability and rebellion.
Game Use: A wardrobe choice opens a story about a mother’s old house and the life she rejected.

Source Detail: The abandoned railcar is lookout, playground, imagined vehicle, and threshold.
Narrative Function: Place can hold escape fantasies for years.
Game Use: The player climbs it to survey the compound; the same framing changes later in the game.

Source Detail: MREs, water purifiers, flint, herbs, and weapons are packed for an expected siege.
Narrative Function: Preparation is both skill and fear.
Game Use: A sibling jokes about an expired MRE while another remembers sleeping with the bag.

Source Detail: Jonah seals a rifle in plastic and buries it beside the railcar.
Narrative Function: A hidden object changes the meaning of a childhood place.
Game Use: Metal detector chatter can reveal different memories of why it was buried.

Source Detail: Ruth returns pale and trembling after assisting a dangerous delivery; later she retells emergencies with more confidence.
Narrative Function: Stories change as fear becomes identity.
Game Use: An apprentice hears the polished version; Mara remembers the trembling version.

Source Detail: A modern phone appears among murky herb jars because the healer’s work requires contact with the outside world.
Game Use: A ringing phone interrupts a doctrine argument and forces practical action.

Source Detail: Mother, father, grandmother, christening, and baptism records disagree about Tara’s birth date.
Narrative Function: Identity requires proof people may not possess.
Game Use: A clerk asks for one date while the family offers three stories.

Source Detail: Jonah catalogues years of pencil shavings while chaos fills the rest of the house.
Game Use: A box found after Jonah leaves triggers music and study memories.

Source Detail: Choir recordings allow a quiet brother and sister to know each other without much speech.
Game Use: Ambient music unlocks a silent optional scene rather than a dialogue wheel.

Source Detail: Jonah feeds three perfectly arranged tacos into Ruth’s tincture juicer to drown out a repeated lecture.
Narrative Function: Absurd action can be resistance without open confrontation.
Game Use: A family meal callback signals Jonah’s humor and fatigue.

Source Detail: Abel contrasts blackened work hands with the grandparents’ clean white carpet.
Game Use: Mara can repeat, question, or reinterpret the phrase after a safe job in town.

Source Detail: A catastrophic burn is retold as a funny story about baling twine and a proper belt.
Game Use: The joke returns at supper, then the journal asks who actually put out the fire.

Source Detail: Abel jokes that officials limiting dog ownership would drown in rain without a roof.
Game Use: The same joke heard later may feel warm, ominous, or manipulative depending on context.
